name: nextjs-subscription-payments
purpose: A Next.js starter template that gives SaaS builders a working subscription business skeleton: Supabase sign-in and Postgres, Stripe Checkout for paid plans, the Stripe customer portal for self-service billing, and webhooks that copy products, prices and subscription status from Stripe into the database.
stage: Sunset template: the README says the repo has been replaced by nextjs/saas-starter. It ships a public demo and a Vercel deploy button and runs in Stripe test mode until the deployer switches to live keys; nothing in the repo shows a live business with real customers.

audiences.name: Developers and founders deploying the template
audiences.description: The primary reader of the README: someone who clicks Deploy to Vercel, connects Supabase and Stripe, and wants to 'earn recurring revenue from your customers'.

audiences.name: End customers (subscribers)
audiences.description: People who sign up on the deployed site, pick a monthly or yearly plan and pay through Stripe Checkout, then manage billing in the Stripe portal.

audiences.name: Business operator
audiences.description: Whoever runs the deployed site: creates products and prices in the Stripe dashboard (or via the fixtures file), configures the customer portal, and switches to live mode.

audiences.name: Platform partners (Vercel, Supabase, Stripe)
audiences.description: The deploy button installs the Supabase Vercel integration and the Stripe client registers itself as an official Stripe plugin (appInfo), so the template also drives adoption of these three platforms.

value.name: Billing plumbing already wired
value.description: Auth, a Postgres schema with row-level security, Checkout, customer portal and webhook sync are done, so a builder starts with a sellable subscription product instead of a blank app.

value.name: Self-serve subscribe and manage
value.description: A subscriber can sign up with password, magic link or GitHub, subscribe in a hosted Stripe page with promotion codes, and later update payment method, switch or cancel in the Stripe portal.

value.name: Catalog managed only in Stripe
value.description: The operator never edits plans in the app: product and price events from Stripe are upserted into Supabase, and the pricing page reads them from there.

money_flows.name: Subscriber pays operator a recurring plan fee via Stripe
money_flows.description: Recurring prices open a Checkout Session in subscription mode for quantity 1. Example plans in the fixtures are Hobby at 10 USD/month or 100 USD/year and Freelancer at 20 USD/month or 200 USD/year; these are test fixtures, and the real prices live in the operator's Stripe account.

money_flows.name: Promotion codes discount the first payment
money_flows.description: Checkout is created with allow_promotion_codes: true, so any coupon the operator defines in Stripe can lower what the subscriber pays.

money_flows.name: Free trial before first charge
money_flows.description: If a price carries trial_period_days of 2 or more, Checkout sets a trial_end; shorter trials are dropped and the default TRIAL_PERIOD_DAYS is 0, so by default there is no trial.

money_flows.name: One-time purchases (half built)
money_flows.description: A one_time price opens Checkout in payment mode, but the webhook only records checkout sessions in subscription mode, there is no orders table, and the pricing page only shows month and year prices. Money could be taken without the app recording what was bought.

money_flows.name: Processing and hosting costs
money_flows.description: Stripe processing fees and Vercel or Supabase hosting costs are not stated anywhere in the repository.

journeys.name: Visit, sign up, get an account
journeys.outcome: A signed-in user with a row in public.users

steps.name: Land on the pricing page
steps.description: The home route renders Pricing with the user, active products and current subscription.

steps.name: Subscribe without an account
steps.description: Clicking Subscribe while signed out sends the visitor to /signin/signup.

steps.name: Sign up
steps.description: Password sign-up, email magic link or GitHub OAuth, all toggled in auth-helpers/settings.ts. An invalid email is flagged but the sign-up call still runs.

steps.name: Confirm and exchange code
steps.description: /auth/callback exchanges the auth code for a session and redirects to /account.

steps.name: Profile row created
steps.description: A database trigger on auth.users inserts the public.users row with full_name and avatar_url.

steps.name: Session kept fresh
steps.description: Middleware refreshes the Supabase session on every non-static request and silently passes through if Supabase is not configured.

journeys.name: Choose a plan, pay, become a subscriber
journeys.outcome: An active or trialing row in subscriptions linked to the user

steps.name: Pick interval and plan
steps.description: Toggle monthly or yearly (only intervals that exist are shown) and click Subscribe on a product card.

steps.name: Find or create Stripe customer
steps.description: createOrRetrieveCustomer looks up the customers mapping table, falls back to finding a Stripe customer by email, else creates one, and writes the mapping.

steps.name: Create Checkout Session
steps.description: Server action builds a session with required billing address, promotion codes, quantity 1, and success URL back to the current path.

steps.name: Pay on Stripe-hosted Checkout
steps.description: The browser is redirected with stripe.redirectToCheckout; card entry and payment happen on Stripe, outside this repository.

steps.name: Webhook records the subscription
steps.description: checkout.session.completed (subscription mode) and customer.subscription.created both call manageSubscriptionStatusChange, which re-reads the subscription from Stripe and upserts it into subscriptions.

steps.name: Copy billing details
steps.description: For new subscriptions, billing details are copied to the Stripe customer and users table, but only when name, phone and address are all present; Checkout does not collect phone, so this usually does nothing.

steps.name: See plan on account page
steps.description: /account shows the plan from the single trialing or active subscription.

journeys.name: Change payment method, switch or cancel
journeys.outcome: Stripe subscription changed and mirrored in Supabase

steps.name: Open customer portal
steps.description: The account page's 'Open customer portal' button calls createStripePortal.

steps.name: Stripe billing portal session
steps.description: A portal session for the mapped customer returns to /account.

steps.name: Change plan or cancel in portal
steps.description: What the portal allows (update payment method, switch, cancel) depends on dashboard settings the README tells the operator to toggle on.

steps.name: Webhook mirrors the change
steps.description: customer.subscription.updated and .deleted upsert the new status, cancel_at_period_end and period dates.

steps.name: 'Manage' on the pricing page
steps.description: When subscribed, product cards say Manage but still start a new Checkout Session rather than opening the portal.

journeys.name: Publish plans and prices
journeys.outcome: Plans appear on the pricing page

steps.name: Create products and prices in Stripe
steps.description: In the Stripe dashboard, or with `stripe fixtures fixtures/stripe-fixtures.json` for the Hobby and Freelancer examples.

steps.name: Webhook upserts products and prices
steps.description: product.* and price.* events upsert or delete rows; a price whose product has not arrived yet is retried 3 times with a 2 second sleep.

steps.name: Pricing page reads active catalog
steps.description: Active products with active prices, ordered by metadata.index and price; products and prices are publicly readable and published for realtime.

journeys.name: Deploy and go live
journeys.outcome: A live-mode deployment taking real payments

steps.name: Deploy to Vercel with Supabase integration
steps.description: Deploy button asks for Stripe keys; the Supabase integration sets env vars and runs the init migration.

steps.name: Configure GitHub OAuth and site URL
steps.description: Set Supabase site URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL; getURL falls back to the Vercel URL and then localhost.

steps.name: Register the Stripe webhook
steps.description: Point Stripe at /api/webhooks with 'Select all events' and set STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, then redeploy.

steps.name: Switch to live mode
steps.description: Archive test products, swap in live keys and a live webhook, redeploy; the code prefers STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_LIVE when set.

systems.name: Next.js app
systems.description: Next.js 14 App Router app: pricing page at /, /account, /signin/[id], /auth/callback, /auth/reset_password and the /api/webhooks route; server actions do checkout, portal and auth.

systems.name: stripe (server SDK)
systems.description: Creates customers, Checkout Sessions and billing portal sessions, verifies webhook signatures and re-reads subscriptions. API version is left unset (null).

systems.name: @stripe/stripe-js (browser)
systems.description: Loads Stripe.js with the publishable key to redirect the browser to Checkout.

systems.name: @supabase/supabase-js and @supabase/ssr
systems.description: Supabase is both the auth provider (password, magic link, GitHub OAuth) and the Postgres database; a service-role client bypasses RLS for webhook writes.

systems.name: supabase CLI
systems.description: Dev dependency used for local Supabase, migrations, type generation and seeding.

systems.name: Supabase Postgres
systems.description: Five tables: users (profile, billing_address, payment_method), customers (private user to Stripe customer map), products, prices, subscriptions; RLS on all, products and prices public-read.

systems.name: Stripe Checkout and customer portal
systems.description: Hosted payment and billing pages; their configuration lives in the Stripe dashboard, not in the repo.

systems.name: GitHub OAuth
systems.description: The only OAuth provider enabled, through Supabase Auth.

systems.name: Vercel hosting
systems.description: Intended host; the deploy button and NEXT_PUBLIC_VERCEL_URL fallback assume Vercel.

evidence.label: first item price, quantity, period dates
email check does not stop signUp

risks.name: Second subscription from the 'Manage' button
risks.description: When a user is subscribed, the pricing cards say Manage but call checkoutWithStripe, so a subscriber can buy a second subscription. getSubscription then uses maybeSingle over all trialing/active rows, which errors on two rows and returns null, so the paying user looks unsubscribed.
risks.signal: Users with more than one row in subscriptions with status active or trialing; Stripe customers with 2+ active subscriptions

risks.name: Webhook rejects most events Stripe sends
risks.description: The README says to subscribe the endpoint to all events, but the handler returns 400 for every event outside its ten, and also for handler errors. Stripe treats non-2xx as failed and retries; sustained failures can lead Stripe to disable the endpoint (Stripe behaviour, not shown in this repo), which would stop all plan and subscription sync.
risks.signal: Webhook failure rate in the Stripe dashboard; 'Unsupported event type' lines in function logs

risks.name: Stripe customer linked by email alone
risks.description: If a user has no customers row, the code adopts the first Stripe customer with the same email. With email confirmation off (it is off in the local config) or an unverified address, a new account could be linked to someone else's Stripe customer and open their billing portal.
risks.signal: Two Supabase users mapped to the same stripe_customer_id; 'Supabase customer record was missing' warnings

risks.name: Subscriptions created outside the app never sync
risks.description: manageSubscriptionStatusChange requires a customers row for the Stripe customer and throws otherwise, returning 400. Subscriptions created in the Stripe dashboard or for customers not made by this app keep failing and retrying.
risks.signal: 'Customer lookup failed' errors in webhook logs

risks.name: One-time payments not recorded
risks.description: A one_time price is charged through Checkout in payment mode, but nothing stores the purchase and the pricing page never shows such prices; any one-time revenue is invisible to the app.
risks.signal: Successful payment-mode checkout sessions in Stripe with no matching database row

risks.name: Unpinned Stripe API version
risks.description: apiVersion is null, so the account's default API version decides the shape of responses. The sync reads subscription.current_period_start/end, quantity and items[0]; if the account version changes these fields, toDateTime could produce an invalid date and the upsert would fail.
risks.signal: Webhook 400s with RangeError or 'Subscription insert/update failed' after a Stripe API upgrade

risks.name: Sunset template on pinned 2024 dependencies
risks.description: The README says this repo is replaced by nextjs/saas-starter; it pins Next 14.2.3, @stripe/stripe-js 2.4.0 and @supabase/ssr 0.1.0, so fixes will not arrive from upstream.

risks.name: Price sync sleeps inside the webhook
risks.description: If a price arrives before its product, upsertPriceRecord sleeps 2 s up to 3 times inside the request, which can hit serverless time limits; a price whose product is an expanded object is saved with product_id ''.
risks.signal: Webhook timeouts on price.created; prices with empty product_id

risks.name: Billing details rarely saved
risks.description: copyBillingDetailsToCustomer returns early unless name, phone and address all exist, and Checkout does not collect phone, so users.billing_address and payment_method likely stay empty. It also runs twice per new subscription (checkout.session.completed and customer.subscription.created).
risks.signal: Share of subscribed users with null billing_address

risks.name: Name change does not show
risks.description: updateName writes Supabase auth user metadata, but the account page reads full_name from public.users, which only the sign-up trigger fills.
risks.signal: Users whose auth metadata full_name differs from public.users.full_name

risks.name: Invalid email still submitted
risks.description: signUp sets an error redirect for an invalid email but does not return, so the Supabase sign-up call runs anyway.
risks.signal: Supabase sign-up errors for malformed emails

risks.name: Users can write their own billing fields
risks.description: The users RLS policy lets a user update their whole row, including billing_address and payment_method, which the app treats as Stripe-sourced data.
risks.signal: Updates to users.payment_method not made by the service role

risks.name: No tests or CI
risks.description: The scan found no CI workflows and the repo has no test files, so none of the money paths above are checked automatically.
risks.signal: Any change to utils/supabase/admin.ts or app/api/webhooks/route.ts shipped without a test run

unknowns.name: Is any deployment live and taking real money?
unknowns.description: The repo only shows a demo URL and test-mode setup; whether this checkout is running in live mode, with how many subscribers, is not in the sources.

unknowns.name: What are the real plans and prices?
unknowns.description: Prices live in the operator's Stripe account; the fixtures are examples and supabase/seed.sql is empty.

unknowns.name: What does a subscription unlock?
unknowns.description: The pricing copy says plans 'unlock additional features', but no code checks subscription status to gate anything; the product being sold is not defined.

unknowns.name: What can customers do in the portal?
unknowns.description: Cancel, switch and payment-method rules are Stripe dashboard settings, not in the repo.

unknowns.name: Production auth settings
unknowns.description: Whether the hosted Supabase project requires email confirmation, and its redirect URLs, are not in the repo (the local config disables confirmation). This decides how serious the email-linking risk is.

unknowns.name: Which Stripe API version the account uses
unknowns.description: The code leaves apiVersion null; the account default is outside the repo.

unknowns.name: Has this fork been changed from the template?
unknowns.description: The checkout is at a README-update commit; nothing shows whether the developer has added their own product on top.

improvements.name: Send subscribers to the portal, not Checkout
improvements.description: When a subscription exists, make the pricing card button call createStripePortal; and make getSubscription tolerate more than one active row (order and limit 1) so a double subscriber still sees a plan.

improvements.name: Acknowledge unhandled events with 200 and subscribe only to the ten used
improvements.description: Return 2xx for events the handler ignores and update the README to select only the relevant events.

improvements.name: Stop linking Stripe customers by email
improvements.description: Create a new Stripe customer (with supabaseUUID metadata) when no mapping exists, or require a verified email and matching metadata before adopting one.

improvements.name: Pin the Stripe API version
improvements.description: Set apiVersion explicitly and add a test fixture for the subscription shape the sync reads.

improvements.name: Decide on one-time prices
improvements.description: Either reject one_time prices at checkout or record payment-mode sessions in a purchases table.

improvements.name: Add webhook and checkout tests in CI
improvements.description: Replay recorded Stripe events against the webhook handler and assert the database rows.

improvements.name: Plan a move to the maintained starter or upgrade dependencies
improvements.description: The README points to nextjs/saas-starter; otherwise upgrade Next, Stripe and Supabase packages.

improvements.name: Small correctness fixes
improvements.description: Return early on invalid sign-up email, write full_name to public.users in updateName, drop the phone requirement in billing copy, restrict the users update policy to profile columns, and remove the in-request price retry sleep.
